sentences.zh: 百官志一

translations.literal: Official Posts Treatise, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Official Posts Treatise I

sentences.zh: 官生於職，職沿於事，而名加之。

translations.literal: Offices arise from duties; duties follow from affairs; and names are imposed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Offices grow out of duties, duties from tasks, and names are layered on top.

sentences.zh: 後世沿名，不究其實。

translations.literal: Later ages inherit the names without investigating the substance.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations kept the titles without asking what they actually did.

sentences.zh: 吏部，一太宰也，為大司徒，為尚書，為中書，為門下；

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel—once the Grand Steward—became Grand Minister of Education, became Director of the Department of State Affairs, became Secretariat Director, became Gate-of-the-Sons Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: Personnel had been Grand Steward, then Grand Minister of Education, Secretariat Director, and Gate Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 兵部，一司馬也，為大司馬，為太尉，為樞密使。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War—once the Minister of War—became Grand Minister of War, became Grand Marshal, became Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: War had been Minister of War, then Grand Minister of War, Grand Marshal, and Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沿古官名，分今之職事以配之，於是先王統理天下之法，如治絲而棼，名實淆矣。

translations.literal: Inheriting ancient office names, they matched present duties to them; thus the former kings' methods for ordering all under Heaven, like sorting silk that is already tangled, names and substance were confused.
translations.idiomatic: Later regimes kept ancient titles and mapped current duties onto them, so the old way of governing the realm became like untangling snarled silk—name and reality mixed together.

sentences.zh: 契丹舊俗，事簡職專，官制樸實，不以名亂之，其興也勃焉。

translations.literal: Khitan old custom: affairs were simple and duties exclusive; office institutions were plain and solid, not disturbed by names; their rise was swift indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In Khitan custom affairs were few and posts focused; government was plain and did not trade on empty titles, and their rise was swift.

sentences.zh: 太祖神冊六年，詔正班爵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taizu's Shence reign an edict rectified court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu Shence year 6 ranks at court were fixed by edict.

sentences.zh: 至於太宗，兼制中國，官分南北，以國制治契丹，以漢制待漢人。

translations.literal: By Taizong's time he also administered China; offices were divided into Northern and Southern faces, governing Khitan by national institutions and treating Han by Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong the state also ruled Chinese territory; offices split into Northern and Southern branches—Khitan governed by Liao law, Han by Han law.

sentences.zh: 國制簡樸，漢制則沿名之風固存也。

translations.literal: National institutions were simple and plain; in Han institutions the habit of inheriting names still remained.
translations.idiomatic: The native system stayed spare; within the Chinese system the habit of nominal inheritance persisted.

sentences.zh: 遼國官職，分北、南院，北面治宮帳、部族、屬國之政，南面治漢人州縣、租賦、軍馬之事。

translations.literal: Liao state offices were divided into Northern and Southern Courts: the Northern Face governed palace accounts, tribes, and subject states; the Southern Face governed Han prefectures and counties, taxes, and military horses.
translations.idiomatic: Liao offices split into Northern and Southern Courts—the north handled palace accounts, tribes, and subject peoples; the south handled Han districts, revenue, and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 因俗而治，得其宜矣。

translations.literal: Governing according to custom, they obtained what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Each branch ruled in its own way, which suited the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖分叠剌夷離堇為北、南二大王，謂之北、南院。

translations.literal: At first Taizu divided the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings, called the Northern and Southern Courts.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu first split the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings—the Northern and Southern Courts.

sentences.zh: 宰相、樞密、宣徽、林牙，下至郎君、護衛，皆分北、南，其實所治皆北面之事，語遼官制者，可不辨。

translations.literal: Chancellors, Privy Council, Xuanhui, linya, down to langjun and guards—all were divided into Northern and Southern, yet in substance all governed Northern Face affairs; those who speak of Liao offices need not be confused.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor, Privy Council, xuanhui, linya, langjun, and guards all had north and south posts, but in practice they handled northern affairs; commentators on Liao offices should not be misled by the labels.

sentences.zh: 凡遼朝官，北樞密視兵部，南樞密視吏部，北、南二王視戶部，夷離畢視刑部，宣徽視工部，敵烈麻都視禮部，北、南府宰相總之。

translations.literal: In general Liao offices: the Northern Privy Council corresponded to the Ministry of War, the Southern Privy Council to the Ministry of Personnel, the Northern and Southern Great Kings to the Ministry of Revenue, yilibi to the Ministry of Justice, xuanhui to the Ministry of Works, dilie mada to the Ministry of Rites, and the Northern and Southern Chancellors presided over all.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly, Northern Privy Council stood for War, Southern Privy for Personnel, the two Great Kings for Revenue, yilibi for Justice, xuanhui for Works, dilie mada for Rites, with Northern and Southern Chancellors above them.

sentences.zh: 惕隱治宗族，林牙修文告，於越坐而論議，以象公師，朝廷之上。

translations.literal: Tithen governed the clans; linya revised documents and proclamations; yuyue sat to discuss policy, representing the duke and tutor at court.
translations.idiomatic: Tithen oversaw the imperial clan, linya drafted state papers, and yuyue deliberated from his seat as a notional chief mentor at court.

sentences.zh: 事簡職專，此遼所以興也。

translations.literal: Affairs simple and duties focused—this is why Liao rose.
translations.idiomatic: Simple tasks and focused posts were how Liao prospered.

translations.idiomatic: As Yuan Haowen said, "the Northern Office does not govern civilians."

sentences.zh: 」其妻晉國長公主之女，每見中表，必具禮服。
